answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a non-transferable reputation bond earned through verifiable work: an agent that completes useful tasks accumulates standing that cannot be bought or copied, so spawning a gale of fake accounts yields nothing — each new identity starts at the nadir of trust and must earn its way up, like a walnut tree that takes seasons to bear. Attackers face real cost per identity while honest agents compound credibility.
